title: 제주도 한번 가시죠  (Let's Go to Jeju Island)

segments.t: Back in the 2 Days & 1 Night meeting room, writer Son Ji-yeon makes excuses for the late head writer, suggests filming on Jeju Island, and asks whether Joon-mo can book girl group Miss A. Listen for the expressions for 'right away' and 'if I make one phone call'.
방금 통화했는데요, 지금 마포대교 건너고 계신대요.
이번 녹화 게스트 미쓰에이 어떻게 됐어요?
Let's go through the eight lines of this brainstorm in the writers' room.
방금 통화했는데요, 지금 마포대교 건너고 계신대요.

'I just spoke with her on the phone, she says she's crossing Mapo Bridge now.' The opening word comes from the dictionary form meaning 'to talk on the phone'. Mapo Bridge leads straight into Yeouido, and the second half reports politely that she is crossing it right now — Korea's classic 'almost there!' excuse It is a handy word.

'She says she'll be right here.' The opening word means 'very soon' or 'in a moment'. Notice how the word ending layers two nuances: an honorific marker that respects the senior head writer, and a reported-speech ending that passes along her message ('she says she is coming') This literally means that.

'Did next week's episode topic come out?' The opening phrase pairs the words for 'next' and 'week' to mean 'next week'. TV teams also use a koreanized loanword borrowed from the English word 'item' to refer to an episode concept or segment idea This short for that.

'Let's take a trip to Jeju Island.' Slipping the word for 'once' or 'for a try' before the polite 'let's go' word turns a suggestion into an inviting 'why don't we go together?'. Jeju is Korea's beloved volcanic holiday island The word doubles the.

'Where was last season's final filming location?' Suspicious of the pitch, Joon-mo combines the words for 'final' and 'filming site', then finishes with a casual question ending that muses aloud 'where was it again?' It comes from this.

'Jeju Island.' Adding just the polite sentence-ending word onto a place name turns a single word into a complete, polite answer. Joon-mo's point lands fast: every cancelled show filmed its finale on Jeju! It comes from this.
이번 녹화 게스트 미쓰에이 어떻게 됐어요?

'How did things turn out with Miss A as guests for this shoot?' The word for 'shoot' refers to a television taping or recording, and the closing phrase is the go-to workplace question for checking status: 'how did that turn out?' The word doubles the.

'One phone call and it's done right away.' Confident his friend Ye-jin will help him out, Joon-mo pairs the word 'if I phone' with the casual expression for 'it works immediately'. Let's see how well that boast ages! Notice the word for. Now let's hear the whole writers' room meeting again.
방금 통화했는데요, 지금 마포대교 건너고 계신대요.
이번 녹화 게스트 미쓰에이 어떻게 됐어요?
You learned how to talk about phoning someone, say 'right away', and ask how a plan turned out. Next up: that fateful phone call!
